question: What price should Anjali mark on a shirt which cost her ₹7,000, so as to gain 17% after allowing successive discounts of 35% and 30%?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Required SP for 17% gain = 7000 × 1.17 = 8190

Successive discounts ⇒ net factor = 0.65 × 0.70 = 0.455

MP × 0.455 = 8190

⇒ MP = 8190 ÷ 0.455 = 18000

**∴ Answer = ₹18000**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

CP = 7000; Gain = 17%; Discounts = 35%, 30%

**Formula used:**

SP = CP × (1 + gain%); SP = MP × (1 − d₁)(1 − d₂)

**Calculation:**

⇒ SP = 7000 × 117/100 = 8190

⇒ Let MP = x

⇒ SP = x × (0.65 × 0.70)

⇒ 8190 = x × 0.455

⇒ x = 8190 ÷ 0.455

⇒ x = 18000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹18000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Discounts

Multiply factors: (1 − d/100)

Profit Formula

SP = CP × (1 + profit%)

Reverse Calculation

MP = SP ÷ (net discount factor)

Key Tip

Always find SP first, then MP
